notes.title: Demo out now!
notes.content:
Demo Released, Feedback Welcomed!

Announced and delivered, a key milestone for my very first game dev project. Even if it's no Balatro or R.E.P.O., still proud that I made it that far. Now it's time to see, how the overall feedback and response will be. Thing will move forward based on the responses...

Glimpse Back in Time, and a Shoulder Pat

Looking back, it has been so far a hell of a journey. Extremely ambitious goals for a self-taught, first time solo dev. But I think it is because of these ambitions that I learned an incredible array of skills in game dev and around it, and feel prepared for any challenges to come. So, no matter how this projects proceeds, it was already a huge win on a personal level...

notes.title: What's up? Where is the Demo? (2nd half of March)
notes.content:
Main Goal: Demo

The demo release remains the main goal #1. At the moment, QA is undergoing in full speed. After a dozen demo builds or so, less and less bugs are found - which hopefully means, that indeed there are not that many left. Basic balancing is done for combat to make sure things work reasonably well. That leaves full confidence, that in 2-3 weeks, it can be released. Prior to that will share more about the scope and content.

Refreshed Look

Artworks were done and delivered by Hollow and Hues. Great like always, I love it and it boosts the whole project to a new level. Thanks for that!

What else?

As QA is the main focus, there is not much else going on at the moment. (Re-)activating some close-to-final features like weapons, maps, weather effects, finalizing and fixing them where necessary. Will wrap things up for the demo release with a fresh new trailer - already feeling, that the last trailer from December 2024 is sooo outdated ːsteammockingː 

... Meanwhile keep posting bits here and there on Discord, Bsky and X/Twitter

notes.title: Demo in March 2025 and 4 Minutes Gameplay Footage
notes.content:
Swamp with Updates

Actually a good thing: I feel there is so much going on, that I think it makes sense to cut the news a bit, and focus just on the most-interesting things - and just mention the rest briefly.

Road to the Demo in March

A small and solid playable demo remains the next big milestone. Currently steps are polishing and debugging. Just like in the weeks before, I remain absolutely confident, that Q1, more specifically march, is absolutely realistic. That's 3-6 weeks from now.

4 Minutes Gameplay Preview

TL;DR: Youtube Link.

This gameplay preview from unreleased footage focuses on the non-combat, such as dialogues, looting, environment and feeling itself. While combat is a big part of the game, it was shown already a lot in previous updates, so this time, things are showing another side of the game.

Refreshed Look

First impressions are important, so Gate Project is in coop with our friends and partners at the design studio Hollow and Hues to spice things up in all directions regarding assets and visuals. A current proposal which is floating around, is the new logo...

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45158465/291aaaf2c56f9df0e672154a8a5e51f1fab92fb0.png

Other

Like announced on top, the rest will just be a footnote here, even though all of it would be worthy to show off in more details:

 new supporting unit type "Special Forces": superior to regular soldiers, agile, quick and deadly on close combat with their SMGs, using the new ability "Run'N'Gun"
 new stationary weapon types: added Blaster MGs and a Blaster Cannon of type "Heavy" - this one has slow-firing, but with a lot of oompf
 new direct controls for units: e.g. sometimes it might make sense to force units to reload their weapons before a next engage
 polish and bugfixes across the board: Stuff, which immediately breaks the immersion like flickering UI etc. was dealt with. It's part of the initiative to have a solid demo
 currently considering to reduce news and updates to bigger, bi-weekly news. That would give a bit less overhead work, though at the same time showing progress less frequently...

notes.title: FAQ and Discord Set Up
notes.content:
FAQ on Website

It is somewhat tricky to explain and showcase the game via pictures and short videos, as it is not a clean "1-genre game". To tackle that, I've setup a FAQ section on the website. 

Discord Setup

Speaking of setup: A Discord server is now up and running and decided to open it up. While the game is still in development and there is no public playable game out, can't hurt to have the Discord already in place for quick questions and so on.

Colors and UI

More color improvements and UI cleanups. Originally it felt like something to do later, but after some really valuable feedback, I pulled that work a bit in. So, started to de-clutter the UI, modernize it a bit and make sure, that visually it is a bit more pleasing.

Demo remains focus

Previous plans like the focus on the Demo development for Q1 remain in place. This is a vital milestone to showcase the game and what to expect.

notes.title: Wishlist Breakthrough, Let's Go!
notes.content:
Wishlists Exploding

It's awesome to see, that Gate Project's wishlist count is taking off like a rocket - a great motivator to stay committed to the development and deliver the best possible game and experience! The numbers itself may be "small", but the trend is going in the right direction, a nice growth curve. For that, many thanks to you all wishlisters!

Polish Things Up

On the dev-side, the focus was to finish and polish the new map, HN Librae b. For that, many new props were introduced, details were added and placeholders were replaced with "release candidate"-worthy items. The goal is clear...

Demo In Q1, Release Later

I had many talks with experienced devs and game industry professionals during the Taipei Game Show, which offered valuable insights and opportunities for self-reflection. The good thing is, that the main goals from the 2025 year-start are fine and still valid. It remains the top priority to get a good playable demo out in Q1. The release though, will push it to Q2. Ultimately the idea is, that the demo and it's feedback will guide further dev...

Other News?
There was another valuable lesson from the game show exhibition, probably the most important one: Small dev -> limit the scope af! It's something, I will continue to hammer into the brain, plans and new ideas to make sure, all the efforts won't be wasted on going off-road with too many new crazy ideas. As such, will also continue to wrap up features/designs/... and not hesitate to remove/postpone half-baked ideas for the greater good.

notes.title: Interactive Elements, Map Sizes and more
notes.content:
Adding Interactive Objects
As part of the out-of-combat work, last week was somewhat sluggish and filled with non-dev occupations, but still managed to make a few interesting additions and progresses.

For example added interactive elements, which will have various purposes like triggering doors, mechanisms and many more. One is for now a mystic "Power Stone", which can be activated, often acting as an incredible energy source.

Some Intermediate Dev Steps

Other than that, adding in parallel various map sizes, templates for it and elaborating a workflow for it, to make sure map additions can happen as quickly and efficient as possible. Currently aiming to have ~8 map sizes ranging from "micro" size, which should take only a few minutes to complete, up to "huge", which will be very likely handcrafted key story missions, taking an hour or so to complete.

Related to that, I'm adding the real/game locations in the Milky Way. Gate Project uses real (potentially habitable) exoplanets and locations as reference, since this adds a lot of authenticity. Finding them in online sources, placing them in the correct in-game map takes quite some effort. Also for that, there might be a way better workflow just around the corner, which I'm evaluating.

notes.title: Hello There, 2025! Upcoming Plans...
notes.content:
What's upcoming?
2025 has arrived, time flies by and it's time to lay out some battle plans for the upcoming time. Thinking about something like following and will move things as needed - given that it is for now a "1 man wolf pack" project, since it's start in June 2024.


 (End of 01-2025) Steam's Real-Time Strategy Fest is coming. For that, might update some of the marketing contents like images and videos, but this has a lower priority
 (End of 01-2025) Taipei Game Show - will be there only as visitor, unfortunately, game won't be presented there
 (Q1-2025) More dev focus on out-of-combat elements, as combat is already pretty fleshed out, except for some bugs.
 (Q1-2025) Including plans to get up a Steam Demo in Q1-2025 - originally idea was to do web-based demos and testing for easy accessibility, but the technical limitations regarding performance and quality are just (too) big. So instead, a regular tech demo on Steam + updates may be the way to go prior the EA release.
 (Q2 2025) During next months will evaluate, if may need to move the EA release to Q2 2025, which will give more time for content additions, polish and bugfixing - as releasing a half-baked product is just lame.
 (After EA Release) Typical after-release care package: bugfixing, taking care of player feedback and topics, first... and second: addition of more content, preferably based on player feedback


What are the devs expectations/plans for the demo and EA release?

 If it's not good, it won't be released, but postponed, period
 If there is not enough content to experience and play, release will be postponed
 Major bugs are a no-go and will get max priority, minor ones will be scheduled for fixing them
 Placeholder GFX, VFX and SFX should be the exception, and not a common thing
 The demo should give a short, representative impression of the game's direction / game-play and be a test for the player, if he wants more of that product
 The EA version shall have all key mechanics to fully play the game, while the content variety and stories will be continuously extended - but adequate at all times to enjoy all mechanics... think of the development history of Rimworld, Minecraft and alike


Any xmas / new year gifts?
Well, the time after xmas was meant to be relaxing to recharge energy and motivation - so not much has happened regarding game dev. Nevertheless, still made a quick, small update - new weapon packs!

notes.title: Merry Xmas and a Happy New Year!
notes.content:
Surprisingly lot happened during last week in and out of the core game dev. Short updates below...

Dedicated Gate Project Website Opened
Lucky find (like with epic loot ːsteamhappyː) was that the domain gate-project.com was still free to be taken. As emergency action, all work was temporarily set on hold to get it up and running with basic info. Just as the Steam store page, it will be from now on frequently updated.

New Trailer
A lot happened since the trailer release in beginning of September. To reflect the latest content and status of the development, a new trailer was released.

Internal Wiki is Expanding
The Gate Project universe is expanding rapidly. As such, to keep the game's main story line and all other elements coherent and in line, the wiki is growing as well. Just to name a few exciting locations, which were added to the plans: Proxima Centauri b, Trappist 1 d, Gliese 667 Cc... 

Gate Project cares about authenticity - as such, preferably real locations are added, which were confirmed to exist by NASA, ESA, ... This way, the game can also educate on a matter or two regarding real-life astronomy. It is an extra effort to go through databases etc., ... but I care.

Real-Time Strategy Fest
Steams Real-Time Strategy Fest is coming in January 20-27 2025. While Gate Project will only appear there as an "upcoming title", it's still a nice achievement to be among there among other titles.

Research, Recruitment, Rewards and More
Regarding game content additions: Out of combat gameplay is a key part of the game. Whether it's research or development of new weapons and technology, it is important, that this one fits to the game - and as such they have been developed with easy extend-ability in mind.

End of Year Journey
Xmas is coming, and new year, too! As such, wish you all the best and a good time!

notes.title: Polishing the Core Experience

All in all, the development keeps picking up speed...

Lastly, as more content is added, it feels like an excellent idea to start with a game wiki. For now it's for internal dev purposes, but once the game is released, the plan is to make it public to repurpose it as a played manual/guide.

notes.title: Gameplay Overview On Steam and Scaling Combat Up
notes.content:
More Units On The Field Without Chaos
"Perfectly balanced, as all things should be" - at least that's the goal, and we're on good terms with it. Got to make sure, that scaling up the combats with more units, abilities and so on does not hurt first and foremost the fun, but also overall balance, performance and so on. 

In this regard, the updates for this week were a success. We're now on good terms with up to regular-sized combats, around 10v10, on micro-sized maps. We're also confident, that 20v20 should work fine as well with larger maps. Ultimately for now, 50v50 and 100v100 battles are the upper limit for the largest missions and maps.

Tactical Slow Motion
Replaced the simple "pause" with a slowmotion effect. It feels like the to-go-solution, striking the perfect balance between not interrupting the overall combat flow, and at the same time allowing enough room to react to new combat situations, if they arise.

All in all, 2 major improvements, which pave the way for next weeks update, which will focus on the HQ with it's mission and unit selections.

Additionally, the Steam page has been updated with a brief summary, roughly outlining what game mechanics and content are to be expected. We hope this helps to provide a better understanding, where this game is heading in terms of gameplay and scope.

notes.title: Unit Behavior Rework: 1 Step Back, 5 Steps Forward
notes.content:
Full Internal Unit Behavior Rework
It was a large task, which was tried to be avoided with "the old system still works - wonky - but works". But it kept breaking, being sometimes unpredictable and hard to debug, so it had to go. A full revamp of the way, how units behave and act, took 3 days (which actually is nothing compared to the current and future benefits). Only during dev of the new Behavior-Tree system, it was actually obvious, how much the old and outdated (FSM) system slowed down everything. Yes, probably could have stayed with FSM and just properly rework it, but honestly, it felt like FSM would hit again the wall sooner than later.

Ultimately, it was totally worth it... after that repair fix, now can focus on new content again.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45158465/a1089f95576c7a71eef439545d58d7a87d1200e4.png

notes.title: Getting used to a planned workflow, focusing on what matters
notes.content:
Stop to drift away

It's too easy to get carried away during gamedev a la "let's improve this on the way" or "got a new idea, will immediately implement it, will be quick". Stopping that and will focus on a more planned, disciplined way. That also helps to keep updates more frequent in all directions: new features, bugfixes, something to show. Hopes are, that this will speed things up significantly.

So, what's new to show?
Unit equipment and customization is of course a thing. So this week, the focus was to build a framework, which will support equipment, skins, cosmetics and more. Started with examples, such as colorful armbands for grouping units and a new laser beam weapon.

notes.title: Combat tests - fluent fights and highly performant updates go hand in hand
notes.content:
The combat-tests were great, and focused on improving not only the feeling and responsiveness of the units, but also ironed out bugs and fully reworked a key element: the unit sensor system.

Questions (and answers) from the play-test

- Is the combat engaging and fun? - Definitely engaging! The cover mechanics work, strategy, positioning is key to win... However, we want to improve on the active abilities, add more variation here.

- Is it fluent, stable and properly working? - Debugged lot's of hiccups, improved responsiveness and ultimately the combat of ~25v25 units ran well (with old sensors, see below for the good news).

- Is it performant? With many units it was okay on a mid-tier PC, but that was not enough. We identified a 3rd party (unit) sensor system as a major slow-down, despite only using sensor updates sparingly. Better optimize it now, as it is vital in so many parts of the game.

New unit sensors, what's behind that?

Took some days and headaches, but we replaced the 3rd party sensor solution with a custom solution, incl. all the modern tech bells and whistles, using multi-threading, Unity's Jobs system and Burst compiler, reaching a really impressive state of the art sensor system, great in scalability. Some interesting numbers on that:

- Old sensors (3rd party): 500 sensors, polling just every 1s, caused frame rate spikes, sluggish unit responsiveness and that was already despite own optimizations on that sensor.

- New sensors (own development, fully tailored to our specific needs): 500 sensors, it barely appears in the analysis tools due to highly efficient code and low CPU load, despite real-time per-frame updates!

- New sensors: for fun, we setup 20.000 (!) sensors, sensors start to appear in the analysis tools.

- For fun, part 2: cranked up the number to 40.000 sensors and still had a stable ~60 FPS rate, in Editor mode (!), thus in build will be higher. (although got to admit, that the speed of polling is throttled then to 0.5s, as we reach limitations on how fast data can be transferred within the engine - the calculations itself still stay within astonishing 100FPS)

We won't have 40.000 units with sensors concurrently on the field, but knowing, that the sensors won't be a bottleneck is a relief. In fact, this allows us to have multiple sensors per unit, giving them different behavior options depending on which sensor got activated: front (view) sensor? close-range sensor? sensor from behind?

notes.title: What's next? Early combat playtests!
notes.content:
Currently working on a playable small combat-orientated test arena. It is meant for a basic check of feeling and performance at this stage of the development.

Questions, which this playtest shall answer are:
- Is the combat engaging and fun?
- Is it fluent, stable and properly working?
